title: Industrial Water: From Provider Plan To Reuse Operation
summary: Follow statewide governance, provider strategy, project-specific wastewater agreements, capital projects, construction, acceptance, reclaimed-water operation, and measured use.
current_state_summary: Phoenix now has a provider strategy, active industrial conservation requirements, a project-specific TSMC wastewater agreement, and a municipal reclamation capital trail, but delivered and measured industrial water outcomes remain open.
current_state: Arizona's management-plan rail establishes industrial conservation, measurement, reporting, and compliance requirements.
Phoenix's 2026 provider update identifies supply sources, drought posture, reliability investments, and regulated drinking-water monitoring.
The TSMC agreement names wastewater conveyance improvements, accepted-flow conditions, customer cost responsibility, and reclaimed-water milestones.
The North Gateway capital record identifies an upstream municipal reclamation project without proving construction completion or operating capacity.
The dossier still lacks a complete facility water balance, accepted conveyance work, operating reclaimed-water plants, measured withdrawals, discharges, reuse, and drought performance.

dependency_stack.current_state: State and Phoenix records identify conservation requirements, source portfolios, drought posture, quality monitoring, and reliability investments.
dependency_stack.boundary: Area-wide rules and provider planning do not establish site-level allocation, hydraulic capacity, service, demand, discharge, or reuse.

dependency_stack.current_state: Phoenix and TSMC define conditional wastewater flows, customer-funded conveyance work, and reclaimed-water milestones.
dependency_stack.boundary: Authorization and agreement terms do not prove completed or accepted infrastructure, operating reuse plants, or a complete campus water balance.

dependency_stack.current_state: Phoenix's capital program provides a named North Gateway reclamation project trail.
dependency_stack.boundary: A capital-program entry does not establish final design, procurement, construction, acceptance, capacity, or service.

dependency_stack.current_state: No current public record closes the loop with facility withdrawals, discharges, reuse volumes, compliance, reliability, or drought performance.
dependency_stack.boundary: Operating claims require accepted assets, metered data, permit compliance, service records, and sustained measured outcomes.

evidence_limits: Drinking-water quality compliance is not evidence of spare industrial capacity.
Accepted-flow terms are conditional and do not prove infrastructure completion or actual flow.
Provider strategy and capital plans do not establish a complete TSMC water balance or long-term regional sufficiency.
next_records: Executed agreement, project permits, construction, inspection, acceptance, and operating records for the conveyance improvements.
Initial industrial reclaimed-water plant operation by June 30, 2028 and later plants tied to fab occupancy and production.
Facility-level withdrawals, discharge, reuse, conservation, compliance, drought, cost, and reliability records.
